title: OOM wave dampener + per-session tombstone compactor to stabilize KV cache across hosted/dedicated/private
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Summary: Multiple customers (hosted, Dedicated enterprise, and one Private on-prem deployment) reported recurring GPU OOM cascades over a 6-week window. The incidents correlate with long-lived chat sessions with heterogeneous sequence lengths, sporadic KV tombstone accumulation, and allocator fragmentation that prevents fast page reclamation under bursty traffic. Symptoms included abrupt worker evictions, degraded tail latency, and failed canaries on Dedicated pools.

Scope: Affects hosted and Dedicated fleet in us-west-2 and eu-central-1; isolated Private customer reported near-identical memory pattern on 4-GPU nodes. Not a single-model issue; reproduces with both causal and chat-style models under mixed short/long token distributions.

Immediate customer impact: Elevated error rates during peak windows (5-20% request failures), long recovery times (minutes-level) requiring manual node drains for some Dedicated customers, and one Private customer had to scale down QPS to avoid repeated OOMs.

Root cause hypothesis: Three interacting factors: 1) allocator slab fragmentation that prevents contiguous backing pages from being returned quickly; 2) KV cache tombstones (stale handles for evicted prefixes) accumulating because the per-session tombstone sweep only runs on background intervals that are too sparse for long-lived sessions; 3) a request burst pattern that creates an "OOM wave" where multiple workers hit transient high memory then fail instead of shedding load.

Why previous mitigations failed: Prior fixes reduced average memory pressure but did not address worst-case waveform bursts and per-session tombstone accumulation under long sessions. Existing compaction runs once every 10 minutes, too coarse for problematic customers.

This ticket: implement an "OOM wave dampener" (request admission/backpressure token mechanism plus fast-path page reclamation) and a per-session tombstone compactor that triggers on session lifecycle events and memory pressure. Goal is to eliminate cascade failures and reduce manual intervention for Dedicated and Private customers.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Run mixed QPS load with 60% short requests (<=64 tokens) and 40% long requests (>=1024 tokens) across 8 concurrent sessions per GPU.
2) Keep sessions long-lived, append small prompts periodically to maintain KV entries.
3) Ramp burst to 2.5x baseline over 30s.
4) Observe allocator fragmentation, KV tombstone growth, and eventual OOM when background compaction does not keep up.
proposed_solution:
1) OOM wave dampener: token-bucket admission at worker boundary that throttles non-critical requests when per-worker RSS crosses a soft threshold. When token bucket drains, requests are steered to fallback lower-memory model variants or queued for short windows (<=200ms). This prevents simultaneous full-buffering across many workers.
2) Fast reclamation path: introduce a lightweight page-return path that coalesces free slabs opportunistically on allocation failure rather than waiting for the heavy compactor. This will be limited to reclaiming small contiguous segments to avoid long pauses.
3) Per-session tombstone compactor: on session inactivity or active eviction events, run a targeted sweep that reclaims tombstones and updates KV index hints. Trigger on either per-session byte-growth thresholds or when global tombstone rate exceeds X/s.
4) Metrics & gating: add canary guard and A/B rollouts: start behind a feature flag for 5% of hosted traffic and selected Dedicated pools; Private customers receive an opt-in patch.
5) Fallback: if fast-path reclamation fails, fallback to conservative auto-eviction policy that reduces maximum KV entries per session.
acceptance_criteria:
1) No repeat OOM cascade in synthetic replay tests that previously reproduced the issue.
2) Tail error rate under mixed-burst workload reduced to <=1% for canary hosts.
3) Tombstone count per session reduced by >=80% within 60s of session inactivity in integration tests.
4) No >200ms p99 latency regression on critical short requests during canary.
5) Rollout plan executed with monitoring alerts and automatic rollback on safety triggers.
rollout_plan:
Phase 0 (canary): deploy feature-flagged binaries to 5% hosted nodes + 2 Dedicated pools + one Private customer (opt-in). Monitor for 24-48h.
Phase 1 (expand): increase to 25% and add additional Dedicated clusters if stable.
Phase 2 (global): full rollout across fleets.
Rollback: disable feature flag and trigger graceful session drain on nodes that saw OOMs. Maintain fallback auto-evict knob active during rollout.
testing_plan: Unit tests for token-bucket admission and fast reclamation invariants. Integration replay harness that replays customer traces (anonymized) for hosted and Dedicated workloads. Chaos test that kills compaction workers to verify fast-path safety. Perf bench to validate p99 latency for short requests. Private deployment dry-run on customer staging node before opt-in.
monitoring_signals: Metrics to watch: per-worker RSS distribution, per-session tombstone_count, eviction_rate, admission_throttle_rate, fallback-evict-rate, request_failure_rate, p50/p95/p99 latency for short and long requests. Dashboards: runtime/oom-wave-dampener and runtime/kv-tombstone-compact. Alerts: OOM cascade detected (>=3 worker OOMs in 2m) and thundering admission throttle (>80% workers throttling).
